names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 octombrie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Οκτωβρίου, «Όσιοι Ανδρόνικος και Αθανασία η συμβία του», with the rank word left off; the page calls her «η συμβία του», his wife.
The bare name out of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2421, headed «Афанасия Тавенская, прп.», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. октобар ст. ст., „Преп. Андроник и супруга му Атанасија“ — Преп. at the head of the line is the venerable grade this corpus puts in `types`, and супруга му, his wife, is how the heading places her rather than a name or a rank, so both come off and the bare personal name is the whole of the form. `foldchk.py` measured it as held by `athanasia-of-aegina` alone before this day; the two-folder fold is read in the `serbian` row’s note and in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs`.

source.text: days.pravoslavie.ru, 9 октября ст. ст. — «Прпп. Андроника и супруги его Афанасии (V).»
source.note: The rank is the alt text of the second of the day's two icons, the plain service, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком», which stands immediately before this line and so belongs to the pair the line names. The day's other icon, a polyeleos, is the apostle James's.

attestations.note: The Russian puts the pair in the fifth century, «(V)», against saint.gr's 540; the `floruit` is left as the Greek page set it and the disagreement is recorded here. The day line names her as «супруги его», his wife, and her own index page gives her the epithet the day line does not: «Афанасия Тавенская», of Tabennisi, which is the convent her life puts her in.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul pe 9 octombrie — «Sfânta Cuvioasă Atanasia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Οκτωβρίου — «Όσιοι Ανδρόνικος και Αθανασία η συμβία του»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», and the entry is the same couple: the well-off husband and wife of Antioch in Syria, he a money-changer, who lost their two children, went on pilgrimage to the Holy Land and then to Egypt, and by common decision became monastics — he in the monastery of the abba Daniel, she in the women's monastery of the Tabennesiotes — and fell asleep in peace. The page states «έζησαν κατά το έτος 540 μ.Χ.», so a `dates` object is proposed from its own words. It records a portion of the relics of each of them at the monastery of Kykkos in Cyprus. The page prints a proper apolytikion that names them both, taken here, and an «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον», the common «Τῆς ἐρήμου πολίτης», which names Andronicus alone and is taken for his folder only. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.10.2026 (9. октобар ст. ст.) — „Преп. Андроник и супруга му Атанасија“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, the second of its two names. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. THE HEADING IS AN ENUMERATED COMPANY OF TWO — Андроник and the wife it names, Атанасија — so §5 counts two names, two folders are owed a row, and the corpus holds both. The quoted line is the one heading, whole, on both rows. `dates` UNTOUCHED ON BOTH, AND THE BOOKS ARE IRRECONCILABLE. The two folders hold `floruit` 540 off saint.gr’s «έζησαν κατά το ἔτος 540 μ.Χ.», while the Russian calendar puts the pair in the fifth century and the folders already record that neither is settled. **This entry opens by dating them to the reign of the emperor Theodosius the Great, which is earlier than both** — and it is the Romanian life’s dating, which this folder’s own first sentence already carries. **An emperor is not a source for a year, a reign is not a date, and three books now disagree three ways**, so the field is not touched at all and the disagreement is recorded here. That is the standing instruction where the books cannot be reconciled. `types` UNTOUCHED at `venerable` on both, corroborated by Преп. No `locations`, no `office`. THE ELDER DANIEL AND THE MARTYR JULIAN TAKE NO ROWS, AND BOTH REFUSALS HAVE A NAMED GROUND. The entry sends Andronicus «код старца Данила у Скиту»; the corpus keeps thirteen folders displayed as a Daniel and **not one of them is of Scetis** — the nearest by name, `daniel-the-egyptian`, is a martyr of one of the Palestinian companies under Diocletian and is a different man — so an identification off a bare forename is refused, as the existing lives already refuse it. And the martyr Јулијан **appears** to Athanasia at the graveyard: an appearance is not a relation. The children, the parents and the emperor’s subjects take no rows. **THE HEADING NAMES HER AS HIS WIFE AND NOT BY A RANK OF HER OWN** — супруга му — which is what saint.gr’s «η συμβία του» says too, and Преп. at the head of the line covers them both. Nothing in that is a type: `venerable` stands and no `office` is written. WHAT IS HERS IN WHAT THE BOOK ADDS. **She died first and her husband followed eight days later**, a figure no other book read for this folder gives. The martyr Julian appeared to **her**, at the graveyard, and the consolation he brought is given its content for the first time — that the children are in the kingdom of God and better off there than with their parents on earth. And it is she, not he, whom this entry places in a women’s monastery at Tabennisiot, which is the house the Greek page calls the monastery of the Tabennesiotes. The entry knows nothing of the monk who called himself Athanasius, of the twelve years in one cell or of the letter under the pillow. THE FOLD THIS ENTRY MADE. `foldchk.py` measured «Атанасија» before this day as `[('athanasia-of-aegina', 'sr')]`, so the fold goes from one folder to two and the key goes into `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in the same commit. The other is the abbess of Aegina, a venerable wonderworker kept on 12 April who died in 860; this is the goldsmith’s wife of Antioch kept on 9 October. Two days, two women. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Σωφροσύνης τὴν χλαῖναν τὴν θεούφαντον, κατεποικίλατε χρόαις τῶν ἱερῶν ἀρετῶν, ὁμοφρόνως ἐν σπουδῇ ἄμφω ἀσκήσαντες, ὅθεν ὑμῶν τὴν σιωπήν, ἡ τρισάγιος ᾠδή, ἐδέξατο ἐν ὑψίστοις, Ἀνδρόνικε σὺν τὴ θεία, Ἀθανασία τὴ Θεόφρονι.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the first hymn on the page of «Όσιοι Ανδρόνικος και Αθανασία η συμβία του», and it names them both.

english.text: You embroidered the God-woven mantle of chastity with the colours of the sacred virtues, both of you living in asceticism with one mind and with zeal; and so the thrice-holy song received your silence in the highest, Andronicus, with the divine and God-minded Athanasia.
